title: User data export: GET /v1/export as NDJSON, and an export command in the CLI
description:
Users keep asking for a copy of their data, and the only way today is to set up a replica and read its SQLite file. This adds a server-side export of the user's current documents.

- `GET /v1/export` (device token, no protocol header, like `/v1/documents`) streams `application/x-ndjson`: one line per document, shaped like `GET /v1/documents/:collection/:id` plus `"type": "document"`, ordered by collection and id, then a last line `{"type":"end","documents":<count>}`. A response without that line is incomplete. Shared `exportLineSchema` describes both line kinds.
- `ExportService` reads the `documents` table in pages of 200 with the existing keyset `listDocumentsPage` (primary key order, index scan) inside one read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction, so an export is one snapshot of the moment of the request even while devices keep pushing. The first page is read before anything is sent, so a database failure or a full house is still an ordinary error answer. After that it is a `Readable` over an async generator: the next page is read only when the response has taken the previous lines, so a slow client slows the export down instead of growing the server's memory.
- Each running export holds a pool connection. `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 2, never more than `DATABASE_POOL_MAX - 1`) caps them per process; beyond it the answer is 503 `unavailable`. An export that could send nothing to its client for `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30 s) is cut off. The connection is rolled back and released when the last page is read or when the stream closes for any reason (end, error, client gone, idle cut-off); from checkout to release an error listener catches the session ending or the connection dropping, so neither goes unhandled. No HEAD route for it.
- Client: `HttpTransport.exportDocuments()` reads the body as a stream and yields documents line by line, checking each line and the final count; `timeoutMs` bounds each wait rather than the whole download. A body cut off in transfer is a `NetworkError`; a missing end line, a malformed line or a wrong count is an `InvalidResponseError`. `WireTransport.requestHeaders` is extracted so both paths send the same headers.
- The command-line client gets `export <file>` (`npm run cli -- export documents.ndjson`), which writes the documents through `<file>.partial` (with backpressure, via `pipeline`) and renames it once the export is complete, so `<file>` only ever holds a whole export.

Tests: `packages/server/test/api/export.test.ts` (content, order, other users' documents left out, 401, a snapshot unaffected by pushes between pages, the connection released when the client disconnects mid-export, a connection reset while the first page is read, the concurrency cap) and `packages/client/test/e2e/export.test.ts` (the CLI against a listening server, and truncated, unterminated and miscounted exports leaving no file). README and `.env.example` updated.
